1. Read the current grid, demonstrations, remaining caps, and feedback. Infer a rule only when supported by examples; verify candidate outputs against demos before submitting.
2. For noisy grids containing a distinctive single-color motif amid zeros and another background color, record the motif's colored-cell offsets from its bounding box. Preserve every other cell, including the original motif and zeros/background at non-motif positions inside the bounding box. Do not assume flood-fill or neighbor propagation: test motif translations when the grid visually consists of noisy background plus one seed object.
3. Use a small script to enumerate translations and construct output grids when manual scanning is error-prone. Validate by matching all demonstrated changed/unchanged cells; account for seed shape, legal translations within bounds, and any rotation/reflection only if supported by demonstrations.
